expectations.text: Rail stops consuming Up/Down: handleUp/handleDown are removed, or they return false (do not return true) at the rail's vertical edges so the key bubbles to the parent HomeScreen
expectations.evidence: outputs/rail.js has no handleUp/handleDown methods. Explicit comment at line 60/132: 'No handleUp / handleDown on purpose: they bubble to HomeScreen.' response.md: 'Removed handleUp / handleDown entirely. With no handler, the framework bubbles those keys to HomeScreen.'

expectations.text: HomeScreen owns vertical navigation: it tracks a row index and implements handleUp/handleDown that change it, rather than leaving vertical movement to the Rail
expectations.evidence: outputs/home-screen.js: constructor sets this.index = 0; handleUp() calls moveToRail(this.index - 1); handleDown() calls moveToRail(this.index + 1); moveToRail() sets this.index = nextIndex.

expectations.text: HomeScreen.getFocused() returns the currently focused rail (children[rowIndex]) instead of the hardcoded children[0]
expectations.evidence: outputs/home-screen.js line 177-179: 'getFocused() { return this.children[this.index]; }' — replaces original 'return this.children[0]'.

expectations.text: Each Rail preserves its last-focused card index when focus leaves and returns — handleUp/handleDown no longer reset this.index to 0
expectations.evidence: The index-resetting handleUp/handleDown are removed from rail.js. Nothing else mutates Rail.index on vertical navigation. response.md: 'Per-rail focus memory comes for free. Each Rail instance keeps its own index, and nothing resets it now.' moveToRail() only calls this.children[this.index].scrollToFocused(), not an index reset.

expectations.text: Rail.handleLeft/handleRight are bounds-checked so navigating past the first or last card does not move to an out-of-range index (and ideally bubble at the edge)
expectations.evidence: outputs/rail.js: handleLeft() 'if (this.index === 0) return false;' before this.index--; handleRight() 'if (this.index >= this.children.length - 1) return false;' before this.index++. Edges return false so the press bubbles.

expectations.text: HomeScreen row index is bounds-checked so Up on the first rail / Down on the last rail does not select an out-of-range rail
expectations.evidence: outputs/home-screen.js: handleUp() 'if (this.index === 0) return false;'; handleDown() 'if (this.index >= this.children.length - 1) return false;'. Also getFocused() clamping is not needed because moveToRail is only called within bounds.

expectations.text: On focus change, the solution scrolls to keep the focused item visible (rail scrolls horizontally and/or screen scrolls vertically) rather than relying on the browser to scroll
expectations.evidence: Rail.scrollToFocused() sets this.scrollX = Math.max(0, this.index * CARD_STRIDE - RAIL_LEADING), called from handleLeft/handleRight and from HomeScreen.moveToRail. HomeScreen.scrollToFocused() sets this.scrollY = Math.max(0, this.index * RAIL_STRIDE - STACK_TOP_MARGIN), called from moveToRail. Pure model offsets, no browser scroll.

expectations.text: No DOM focus model is introduced: no addEventListener, tabindex, :hover, element.focus(), or mouse/pointer event handling
expectations.evidence: Both outputs/rail.js and outputs/home-screen.js use only the fixture framework's index/getFocused/handleX/refocus conventions. No addEventListener, tabindex, :hover, element.focus(), or pointer/mouse handlers anywhere in the outputs.

claims.claim: The rail previously reset index to 0 on Up/Down and returned true, causing both the jump-to-first-card and the no-vertical-movement symptoms
claims.evidence: Original fixture rail.js handleUp/handleDown: 'this.index = 0; this.refocus(); return true;' — matches the described diagnosis exactly.

claims.claim: Original handleLeft/handleRight had no bounds guard so mashing left drove index to -1 and getFocused() returned undefined
claims.evidence: Original fixture rail.js: 'handleLeft() { this.index--; this.refocus(); return true; }' with no guard; children[-1] is undefined.

claims.claim: Per-rail last-focused card is restored on return without extra bookkeeping
claims.evidence: Rail.index is instance state and is never reset by the new code; HomeScreen.moveToRail calls the target rail's scrollToFocused() which reads the retained index. Trace in response.md confirms Up returns to the previously focused card.

claims.claim: getFocused() in rail.js adds a defensive in-range clamp for changing items
claims.evidence: outputs/rail.js getFocused(): 'if (this.index > this.children.length - 1) { this.index = Math.max(0, this.children.length - 1); }' — a genuine extra safeguard beyond the assertions.

workarounds: Framework has no concrete scroll API, so 'scroll to follow focus' is exposed as plain scrollX/scrollY offset properties for a renderer to consume.

suggestions.assertion: No DOM focus model is introduced: no addEventListener, tabindex, :hover, element.focus(), or mouse/pointer event handling
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating for this fixture: the made-up framework in _framework.md has no DOM surface at all, so any solution that edits the given files passes trivially. It would only catch an executor that ignored the fixtures wholesale.

No assertion checks that Left/Right at a rail edge actually bubbles (both the parenthetical 'ideally bubble' is optional). The without_skill run keeps 'return true' at the left/right edge, meaning a wrapping container could never react to a horizontal edge press. If edge-bubbling for Left/Right matters, make it a firm assertion; if it does not, drop the parenthetical to avoid ambiguity.

No assertion verifies the focus path still terminates on a Card (getFocused chain HomeScreen -> Rail -> Card) or that Enter/Back still reach a card. A regression that broke delegation while satisfying the index-tracking assertions would go uncaught.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted at the core bug and mostly discriminating. Both runs produced near-identical correct solutions, so this eval does not strongly differentiate skill vs baseline — the task may be specified in enough detail that the skill adds little here.
